title: Zheng et al. 2023, Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
claim: Position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases; 'GPT-4 favors itself with a 10% higher win rate; Claude-v1 favors itself with a 25% higher win rate'; 'our study cannot determine whether the models exhibit a self-enhancement bias' (both quotes rechecked verbatim by the decider 2026-11-21).

title: Panickssery et al. 2024, LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
claim: Abstract read: evaluators score their own outputs higher than humans rate them; models recognize their own text with non-trivial accuracy; fine-tuning shows a linear correlation between self-recognition and self-preference, suggested causal.

title: Verga et al. 2024, Replacing Judges with Juries: Evaluating LLM Generations with a Panel of Diverse Models (PoLL)
claim: Abstract only: "using a PoLL composed of a larger number of smaller models outperforms a single large judge, exhibits less intra-model bias due to its composition of disjoint model families, and does so while being over seven times less expensive." No numeric size for the bias reduction in the abstract.

title: Wataoka, Takahashi, Ri 2024, Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
claim: Full text (arXiv HTML v1). Pairwise comparison with swapped positions on Chatbot Arena dialogues, eight judges. Demographic-parity bias: GPT-4 0.749, Vicuna-13b 0.382, GPT-3.5-turbo 0.191, others near zero or negative. Mechanism: LLMs rate lower-perplexity outputs higher than humans do "regardless of whether the outputs were self-generated"; the factor is "not whether the response is their own but rather the perplexity of the responses." Caveats: GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 perplexity unavailable; scores do not account for intrinsic quality.

title: Self-Correction Bench: Uncovering and Addressing the Self-Correction Blind Spot in Large Language Models (arXiv 2507.02778)
claim: Abstract only. The same error injected as external (user) or internal (model) context: "Testing 14 open-source non-reasoning models reveals a 64.5% Self-Correction Blind Spot: models correct external errors but fail on identical internal ones"; appending "Wait" reduces it by 89.3%. Self-correction, not a cross-family judge.

title: arXiv 2601.22548 (2026), on whether LLM evaluators' self-preference is narcissism or an evaluator-quality confound
claim: Abstract only, read through a summarising fetch. Against an evaluator-quality baseline, "only 51% of examples in previous findings retain statistical significance", covering "89.6% of total self-preference probability mass"; evaluators may prefer their own outputs partly because they answer questions they fail on.
